findings.description: Requirement body and the pane-keyboard trace Notes both assert that TC-6601, TC-6602 and TC-6606 target the .status-prefix markup of the unmounted StatusBar and therefore cannot pass. Verified false for TC-6602: pane-keyboard.spec.ts:23-28 contains no .status-prefix locator at all — it calls pressCtrlB, page.keyboard.press('Shift+5') and verifyPaneCount(page, 2). '.status-prefix' occurs exactly once in frontend/src (StatusBar.tsx:20) and is referenced only by TC-6601 (12) and TC-6606 (18,20). Consequence: disposition A as written ('StatusBar 를 실제 렌더 경로에 마운트하고 prefixMode 상태를 연결해 세 테스트를 그대로 통과시킨다') cannot make TC-6602 pass — 'prefixMode' is referenced nowhere outside StatusBar.tsx, and no Ctrl+B prefix handler or '%'/split-vertical shortcut exists anywhere in frontend/src, so mounting StatusBar leaves TC-6602 red. AC-4 likewise ties disposition A only to StatusBar reachability, which is insufficient for TC-6602.
findings.suggested_action: Split the requirement statement: TC-6601/TC-6606 fail because .status-prefix is never rendered; TC-6602 fails for a different, separately stated reason (the Ctrl+B prefix + '%' split shortcut is not implemented). Either scope this requirement to the two .status-prefix tests, or state a per-test cause and make the disposition menu per-test rather than blanket.

findings.description: Both regression-only Requirement trace rows are present with the correct relation and correct targets (REL-BGSTAB-017 -> REL-BGSTAB-009, REL-BGSTAB-018 -> REL-BGSTAB-011), and no 'supersedes' relation is used anywhere in the 14 new blocks. However the Notes cell of both rows is '-'. The violated AC identifiers appear only in free prose (REL-BGSTAB-017 Requirement/Rationale/Verification Method cite REL-BGSTAB-009 AC-7/AC-8; REL-BGSTAB-018 Rationale cites REL-BGSTAB-011 AC-6/AC-9), not in the structured field a consumer would read.
findings.suggested_action: Fill the Notes cell of each regression-only row with the violated AC ids, e.g. 'Implementation regression against REL-BGSTAB-009 AC-7/AC-8; the contract itself is unchanged.' and 'Implementation regression against REL-BGSTAB-011 AC-6/AC-9.'

findings.description: Trace Note claims terminal-context-menu-registered-items.spec.ts is a 'second existing spec that asserts the not-disabled state only'. Verified false: that spec never asserts a disabled state for the helper textarea — its only reference is `page.locator('.terminal-view:visible .xterm-helper-textarea').first().focus()` at line 31, and its single 'disabled' match (line 176) is a context-menu item, unrelated to the input gate. Conversely the spec that does assert the gate snapshot (terminal-keyboard-regression.spec.ts, reading `captureAllowed` and asserting `disableStdin: false` at 759/767) is not traced at all. The requirement's core claim is still sound: no test anywhere asserts helperDisabled===true or disableStdin===true.
findings.suggested_action: Drop the terminal-context-menu-registered-items.spec.ts trace row (or correct its Note to 'focuses the helper textarea only; asserts nothing about disabled') and add frontend/tests/e2e/terminal-keyboard-regression.spec.ts:759-767 as the real existing not-disabled control.

findings.description: Normative Acceptance Criteria AC-1 through AC-5 all spell the subject as '캐프처' instead of '캡처'. The defect was patched by adding an Erratum bullet inside Implementation Notes ('AC-1~AC-5 의 모든 캐프처 를 캡처 로 읽는다') rather than by correcting the AC text itself, leaving the binding contract text wrong and the correction in a non-normative section. This is the clearest residue of the interrupted authoring run; the Change Notes table still shows only the 'Created' row.
findings.suggested_action: Correct '캐프처' to '캡처' in AC-1..AC-5, delete the Erratum bullet from Implementation Notes, and record the correction as a Change Notes row instead.

findings.description: Neither requirement records the materiality condition of the original defect — that the fencing gate is live in production. acceptRetainedTerminalMutationIdentity opens with `if (retained.mode !== 'shadow') return true;`, i.e. every rejection path in scope is reachable only while shadow mode is on, and shadow mode is unconditionally active in production. Without that statement a reader (or a future implementer weighing priority) cannot tell whether the 'server-error' flattening and the pre-fencing capture gap are live user-visible behaviour or a dormant branch.
findings.suggested_action: Add one sentence to the Rationale of REL-BGSTAB-018 (and cross-reference it from OBS-BGSTAB-007) recording that retained.mode==='shadow' is unconditionally active in production, with the SessionManager.ts:2976 early-return as evidence.

findings.description: AC-7 reads '게이트 도입 시점에 통과 불가 상태로 방치된 테스트가 없어야 하며, 도입 직후 CI 테스트 job 이 실패하지 않아야 한다.' The first clause is an unbounded global negative over the whole test corpus — no automated check can decide it, and the requirement supplies no bounded scope (e.g. 'the specs named in OPS-BGSTAB-003'). The second clause reintroduces exactly the CI-execution self-reference the Requirement body rules out as the verification basis ('검증의 자기참조를 피하기 위해, 이 요구는 CI 실행 결과가 아니라 워크플로 YAML 을 파싱하는 정적 메타 테스트로 검증한다'), and the Verification Method then admits it back as '보조 증거'.
findings.suggested_action: Bound the first clause to the specific tests closed out by OPS-BGSTAB-003 (already a depends_on trace) and either drop the second clause or move it out of the AC into the Verification Method as the supplementary evidence it is described as.

findings.description: Every one of the 14 new requirements carries `Risk | medium`, from the documentation-only OPS-BGSTAB-001/OPS-BGSTAB-004 (explicitly no behaviour change) to REL-BGSTAB-016 (silent loss of user keystrokes with zero feedback in the production default state). Priority does discriminate (high/medium), but the Risk field carries no information and cannot be used to order work.
findings.suggested_action: Re-rate Risk per requirement, or state in the scope section that Risk is not used as a discriminator in this batch.

findings.description: The five new inference markers are written as `[INFERRED:med:advisory]`, while the five pre-existing markers in the same document are `[INFERRED:advisory]`. No marker grammar is defined in docs/rule/SRS-MD-Rules-v2.5.0.md or docs/spec/90.appendix.md, so the added `med:` confidence segment is an undocumented divergence from the only precedent in the file. validate_spec does not flag it.
findings.suggested_action: Either normalise to the existing `[INFERRED:advisory]` form or document the three-segment grammar in docs/spec/90.appendix.md.

findings.description: AC-6 ('세 테스트를 삭제하는 방식은 이 요구를 충족하지 않는다') is a verbatim restatement of the scope constraint already in the Requirement body, not a decidable proposition about the resulting system state. It duplicates a constraint that AC-1 already binds.
findings.suggested_action: Remove AC-6 and keep the deletion prohibition in the Requirement body, or reformulate it as a state proposition (e.g. 'the three test ids remain present in pane-keyboard.spec.ts after the change').
